scope: SP1 CPU execution only (no setup, no proving) of the guest built from this tree, over synthetic conservation-consistent pre-states; public synthetic test data only; no chain, RPC or service contacted. Two builds of the same program sources are measured: the software-keccak build and the keccak precompile build

Session 2 (both precompile builds, every precompile run and the software re-runs at 8,000 to 20,000): the same host with lighter load, load average about 1.4 to 2.6 when sampled after the runs; wall times of the two sessions are not comparable

size_mapping.rule: H (tree leaves + spent nullifiers) a multiple of 80; unspent notes N = H/5; positions P = H/10 over 4 markets; tree leaves L = (H + N)/2 = 3N; spent nullifiers F = H - L = L - N (every spent note left one nullifier)
size_mapping.why: Per batch the keccak work is about 4 permutations per tree leaf (each of the two state roots hashes every leaf and its tree node), 1 per spent nullifier (the decode rebuilds the nullifier chain), and about 2.4 per unspent note and 2.8 per position (the notes and positions digests in the two roots); the counted runs match this to 0.1% (355,413 measured against 355,200 at H = 100,000, phase 0). With L = (H + N)/2 and F = (H - N)/2 that is about 2.5 H + 3.9 N + 2.8 P permutations, increasing in H, N and P. The three admission bounds are enforced separately, so a state with all three at their bounds is the costliest one they admit; that is the shape measured, with N = H/5 and P = H/10, the ratio the measured gateway bounds keep
size_mapping.pre_state: 4 fee-bearing markets at 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 / 2,500 USD with a recorded price and a non-zero stored funding rate and carry; traders 2k and 2k+1 hold opposite positions of 0.01 to 0.05 base, equal entry (within 1% of the price) and funding entry, 50 to 62 USD collateral, in every market; note amounts 50 to 146 USD; reserves 5,000 insurance, 2,000 treasury, 1,000 clearing pool; external_in balances the conservation identity; tree depth 24; wind-down recipient set

batches.phase0: Deposit, Fill (taker buys 0.02 from a resting maker, growing both positions), Fill (partial reverse of 0.01), Withdraw to L1, AccrueFunding x2; 4 timed ops in 700 ms, oracle transcripts signed by the public test key
batches.phase1: SettleAll over the whole state at the recorded prices, no shortfall: every position closes inside its collateral and the 8,000 USD of reserves are paid to the wind-down recipient as one withdrawal leaf
batches.phase1-haircut: SettleAll with every market's recorded price at twice the entry level and empty reserves: the short side's losses exceed its collateral, the pro-rata haircut reissues every unspent note, and the tree gains N leaves before the post-state root

software.method: tree-depth differential: one leaf, no ops, depths 8/36/64; each level adds one 65-byte MerkleNode hash to decode and to each of the two state roots

precompile.method: tree-depth differential: one leaf, no ops, depths 8/36/64; each level adds one 65-byte MerkleNode hash to decode and to each of the two state roots

calibration.note: the calibration differential isolates the cost of one 65-byte node hash: 8,040.3 cycles and 7,643.4 gas in the software build, 1,608.3 cycles and 2,670.8 gas in the precompile build

cost_metric.definition: cost-equivalent cycles. For the software build they are its cycles. For the precompile build they are the software build's cycles for the same witness, scaled by the measured gas ratio: cycles_software x gas_precompile / gas_software
cost_metric.why: the executor counts a KECCAK_PERMUTE syscall as one instruction, so the precompile build's cycle count leaves out the work of proving the permutation; SP1's gas, its estimate of proving cost, includes it. The rate R below is a rate in plain RISC-V cycles, so the precompile build's cost is converted to the cycles of RISC-V code with the same gas. Its gas per cycle is 1.30 to 1.60, against 0.95 to 0.98 for the software build

precompile_projection.method: Effective cycles if every counted keccak-f permutation ran as SP1's KECCAK_PERMUTE syscall: cycles x (gas - permutations x saving) / gas. saving = gas of the 6,437 tiny_keccak::keccakf instructions at the gas-per-cycle of keccak code (from the calibration) minus the syscall's gas from SP1 6.1.0's own cost tables (sp1-core-executor utils::cost_and_height_per_syscall with artifacts/rv64im_costs.json, vm/gas.rs complexity mapping, report.rs normalization 191). Absorb, padding and loop code around the permutation stay in software. A projection only: the precompile build needs a network fetch and is measured when it is built
precompile_projection.status: superseded: the session-1 projection, made before the precompile build existed; the measured build replaces it

gpu_time_model.formula: T(H) = fixed_s + cost(H) / R, cost in cost-equivalent cycles; a size fits when T(H) <= prover_budget_s / margin for phase0, phase1 and phase1-haircut
gpu_time_model.prover_budget_source: crates/gateway/src/prover_client.rs: PROVER_TIMEOUT_SECS, default 900 s, bounds each /prove call. crates/gateway/src/l1.rs min_anchor_timeout_ms: the boot handshake requires anchorTimeoutMs >= (2 x FINALITY_BUDGET + PROVER_TIMEOUT_SECS + 300 s) x 1000, FINALITY_BUDGET = 1,200 s (crates/gateway/src/clock_wait.rs). The launch anchor_timeout_ms is 3,600,000 (docs/REDEPLOY-CC-RUNBOOK.md, docs/RELEASE_MANIFEST.md), which admits at most 3,600 - 2,400 - 300 = 900 s of proving
gpu_time_model.fixed_source: the recorded Groth16 wrapping stage of the clock-v2 proof: container 2026-10-09T18:27:56.49Z to 18:32:06.25Z, 249.8 s with 4 CPUs and 13 GB (docs/audits/2026-10-09-clock-final/generation.json, .github/workflows/clock-proof-wrap.yml); its input is the constant-size recursion output, so it does not grow with the program
gpu_time_model.rate_assumption: No GPU proving throughput is recorded in this repository. R, the sustained core-plus-recursion proving rate of the launch prover in guest cycles per second, is assumed at 1,000,000 (central) with the sensitivity rows below. The central value is taken at the low end because the hard cap protects a one-shot wind-down proof and is raised only by a measured rate
gpu_time_model.recorded_reference: contracts/integration/fixtures/clock-v2-verified records a real proof of a 6,035,092-cycle clock-v2 execution under SP1 6.1.0; its core and recursion time is not recorded

recommendation.basis: Measured on the precompile build, which the program adopts. At the central rate the launch budget allows 200,000,000 cost-equivalent cycles per proof ((900 s / 2 - 250 s) x 1,000,000 cycles/s). The shortfall variant of phase 1 is the costliest batch at every measured size and sets the cap: at 13,280 history it takes 198,828,755 cost-equivalent cycles (129,942,028 cycles, 188,853,499 gas), at 13,360 it takes 200,064,036. Phase 0 and the solvent phase 1 alone would allow about 16,800 and 17,600. Positions and notes keep the measured ratio, H/10 and H/5, and the soft cap is 80%
recommendation.precompile_decision: Adopted. The software build's cap is 5,280; the precompile build's is 13,280, 2.5 times larger. Per 65-byte hash the precompile build takes 1,608 cycles and 2,671 gas against 8,040 and 7,643; across the gate sizes it takes 3.6 to 4.3 times fewer cycles and 2.4 to 2.6 times less gas
recommendation.planned_scale: At the launch prover budget, 100,000 history needs a measured R of at least 7.7 M cycles/s with the precompile (19.0 M with software keccak). The cap scales linearly with R and with the compute seconds per proof, (anchorTimeoutMs / 1000 - 2,700) / 2 - 250; a launch with a larger anchorTimeoutMs gives a proportionally larger cap without a program change

gpu_day: GPU day re-measures: it proves phase 0, phase 1 and the shortfall variant at the configured cap on the launch prover, records the proving time and the sustained rate R, and re-derives the cap with the same formula from the measured rate. This gate fixed the program decision (the precompile) before the program key freezes; the caps are admission policy and change without a new program key
